scope: Root cause of Kablooey's system task queue overflow, and the execution-budget ratio the core now exposes. No Kablooey run was performed for this record.

failure.symptom: service_system_task: System task queue full, then Resetting!
failure.consequence: The later BlobDB 0xb1db install times out because the watch has reset

mechanism.coreBehavior: board_step_before advances device time by the executing instruction's estimated cycle cost, so the guest spends exactly one instruction-cost per board cycle. The generic board's SYSCLK is 64 MHz, giving the guest 64,000,000 estimated cycles per virtual second and no more.
mechanism.audioDrain: QEMU's pebble_audio drains on a 10 ms QEMU_CLOCK_VIRTUAL timer and raises IRQ 10 to request a refill. Ten virtual milliseconds is 640,000 ticks at 64 MHz.

budgetBetweenRefills.basis: 9,619,751 steps per virtual second, measured over a 20 virtual second unchanged qemu_emery 4.37.0 boot

mechanism.reference: Native QEMU's default mode runs the CPU unthrottled, so between two drains the guest completes as much work as the host can execute, not 96,198 instructions. The declared SYSCLK is a timer frequency there, not an execution budget.
mechanism.corroboration: The repository's own earlier observation that native QEMU completed this workload under default wall-clock execution but overflowed under instruction-count pacing. Instruction-count pacing is the same one-cost-per-cycle coupling this core implements, so the reference implementation reproduces the failure when it is paced the way this core is always paced.
mechanism.conclusion: The overflow follows from deterministic 64 MHz pacing rather than from a defect in the audio device, the CPU or the scheduler. It is what a one-instruction-cost-per-cycle model produces for a workload that needs more execution between device events than the budget allows.

change.added: PebbleBus::instructions_per_cycle, the instruction-costs the interpreter completes per board cycle
change.defaultMeaning: Unchanged behavior, equivalent to native QEMU under -icount
change.equivalence: All three 20 virtual second 4.37.0 boots stay byte-identical at the default: same steps, cycles, frames and frame, RAM and UART digests
change.notCheckpointed: The ratio is configuration, not guest state; a restored bus takes the default and its caller re-applies any other setting. At the default the carried remainder is always zero, so the checkpoint format is unchanged.

notDone.kablooeyRun: Not reproduced. The Kablooey 1.0.0 PBW (sha256 7eb911a829a289f92deb75ab5ddabf82b9d13f45947749192e031ec553646dca) comes from apps.repebble.com, and both that host and appstore-api.repebble.com are refused by this environment's network policy.
notDone.whatWouldConfirm: Run the documented fidelity scenario with the PBW at the default ratio to reproduce the 7.102 s overflow, then at a higher ratio. If the overflow moves later in proportion to the ratio and clears once the budget exceeds Kablooey's demand, the cause above is confirmed; if it persists at a large ratio, the cause is elsewhere and this record is wrong.

limits: The mechanism is established from the pinned QEMU source and this core's pacing arithmetic, not from a Kablooey run
No ratio other than 1 has recorded evidence; a run at another ratio is a modeling assumption, not a compatibility result
The estimated cycle cost is neither a retired instruction count nor a physical clock measurement, so the 96,198 figure describes this model, not silicon
Raising the ratio trades away the claim that device time matches the declared 64 MHz SYSCLK; it is an investigation control, not a default
